sections.h2: How do I reach the Mahoning County Recorder?
sections.html:
Walk in at 120 Market Street, Youngstown, OH 44503, on the building's first floor. Counter service runs weekdays from eight in the morning until half past four, while the basement self-serve room closes at four. Dial 330-740-2345 for the office or send a fax to 330-740-2347.

Employees will pull a copy when you can name the recording details, yet they do not run searches for the public. Anyone who must look something up can sit at one of thirteen public terminals or use the online index. Legal advice is not offered by phone or at the desk.

Online searching runs on a system the recorder calls Laredo Anywhere, with a basic search link and a professional one. The page says the web version will eventually replace the older desktop program on the office terminals. An owner tracing an old deed, or checking that a mortgage release was ever filed, can begin there and then ask for a copy using the recording reference the search returns.

At the counter you pay with a check or cash, because the fee schedule rules out credit cards. Documents sent by mail are returned when the check exceeds the exact recording charge, so verify the amount first.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed cost in Mahoning County?
sections.html:
The recorder explains that every charge is set by state law. A posted notice says Senate Bill 94 added $5.00 to most recording charges beginning January 1, 2026. Figures in the table come straight from the county's schedule and assume the paper meets the state layout rule.

Recorder charges quoted from the county's published fee schedule
ServiceCharge listed
Deed, mortgage, lease and similar records$39.00 covers pages one and two, then $8.00 per further page or side
Marginal notation (release, assignment, re-recording)Standard fee and another $4.00 per notation
PlatTen cents a square inch, with a $40.00 floor
Certified copy$2.00 a page and $1.00 to certify
Uncertified copy$2.00 a page
Military discharge (DD214)No charge
Paper that breaks the layout ruleAdditional $20

A short two-page warranty deed falls under the first line. A long legal description or attached exhibit adds pages, and each one adds cost. Smaller lines in the same schedule include $5.00 to file a federal tax lien, $3.00 to release one, $4.00 to release a personal property tax lien, and $50.00 for a zoning resolution. A seller whose title search turns up an old lien should ask the recorder whether a release is on file, because a missing release can hold up a closing.

sections.h2: What must the Auditor approve before a Mahoning County deed can be recorded?
sections.html:
Start at the auditor's counter. The published checklist says an incomplete deed comes back with all its attachments for correction. What the auditor looks for:

  • Whether the grantor is married, single or signing with a spouse
  • Where the buyer wants tax bills mailed
  • The legal description, tied back to the previous deed
  • Seller and spouse signatures, plus a notary clause and stamp
  • Who drafted the deed, with contact information
  • A finished state form: DTE 100 for a sale, or DTE 100 EX for a transfer with no payment

Leave a contact name and phone number with the drop-off. The auditor wants a separate check for each transaction, payable to the Mahoning County Treasurer, and will not take a blank one. On a sale the checklist charges $1.00 per $1,000 of price as the conveyance fee, adds $3.00 per $1,000 as a permissive fee, and tacks on 50 cents for each parcel. An exempt transfer owes just the parcel charge. For questions call 330-740-2010 and press 0.

Land measured in acres, a slice of a platted lot or an outlot needs one extra visit first. The GIS and Tax Map desk, in the lobby at 21 West Boardman Street, signs off before the auditor moves the parcel. The recorder sees the deed only once the auditor has stamped it.

sections.h2: Which layout rules can add $20 to a deed?
sections.html:
A state standardization law has applied since mid-2009, and the recorder enforces it on ordinary deeds. A page that ignores it is still taken, but with a $20 surcharge. The recorder's rules:

  • Print no smaller than a 10 point font
  • Sheets from letter size up to legal length
  • Dark ink only, in black or blue, and no highlighter
  • A margin of one inch down both sides and along the bottom
  • Three blank inches above the text on page one, reserved for office stamps
  • Inch-and-a-half headroom on every page after the first

Court and tax authority papers, plats, DD214 forms, state or federal documents, and anything signed before the law began are exempt. The recorder's home page also carries a notary fraud alert. A title company that prepares the package normally takes care of all of this.

sections.h2: Can I file a deed online in Mahoning County?
sections.html:
Yes, for deeds, mortgages and related papers. The recorder names three vendors:

  • ePN, 888-325-3365
  • Simplifile, 800-460-5657
  • CSC eRecording Solutions, 866-652-0111

Title companies and lenders tend to use these services, which skips the drive downtown and the no-card rule at the counter. A family member handling a quitclaim is more likely to bring paper. Both routes still require the auditor's stamp before recording.

sections.h2: What does the Mahoning County market look like?
sections.html:
The county measures 425 square miles, about 14 of them water, and touches Trumbull, Portage, Stark and Columbiana counties as well as two in Pennsylvania. Named for the Mahoning River, it was formed in 1846. Youngstown, the seat, grew as a center of American steelmaking. Mercy Health, the Youngstown school system and the county government led the list of employers in the county's 2019 financial report.

In QuickFacts, owned homes carry a midpoint value of $154,700 for 2020 to 2024, owners live in 70.3 percent of the housing, and household income at the midpoint is $56,942. Builders took out 174 permits in 2025. Headcount dropped from 238,823 in 2010 to 228,614 a decade later. The 2020 census counted 107,989 housing units, 9.3 percent of them vacant, and found 84.4 percent of residents living in urban areas. Twenty school districts cover the county, including Austintown, Boardman, Canfield, Poland, Springfield and Struthers, so a deed for a house in any of them is filed in this one Youngstown office. Cities such as Youngstown, Struthers, Campbell and Canfield and villages such as Sebring, Poland and Lowellville all record in the same office.

sections.h2: What should a seller settle before filing?
sections.html:
Each item below is a call to a different office:

  • Ask the treasurer, at 330-740-2460, for the unpaid balance on the parcel
  • Get a recorded release from any lender whose loan was paid off
  • Look for liens at the recorder, since mortgages, judgments and mechanic's liens never show on a tax bill
  • Ask the probate court who has authority to sign after an owner's death
  • Compare the legal description in your old deed with the auditor's parcel record

A cash sale follows the same path: the auditor first, then the recorder.

faqs.q: What number reaches the Mahoning County Recorder?
faqs.a: 330-740-2345. Faxes go to 330-740-2347, and the counter is staffed on weekdays.

faqs.q: Does the recorder accept credit cards?
faqs.a: No. The fee schedule lists check or cash only. People who file electronically pay through their vendor.
Yes. A county notice says Senate Bill 94 added $5.00 to most fees from January 1, 2026, and the schedule now shows $39.00 for a deed's first two pages and $8.00 for every page after.

faqs.q: Does the auditor see the deed before the recorder?
faqs.a: Yes. The auditor reviews the deed and collects the transfer charges, and then the deed goes to the recorder. A deed lacking a required item is sent back.

faqs.q: Is a military discharge copy free?
faqs.a: Yes. The schedule lists military records, including the DD214, at no charge and cites Ohio Revised Code section 317.24(A).
